environment.description: Same Ktor service deployed inside a minimal container with a pivot_root(2) into /srv/jail at process start via a custom entrypoint wrapper. The jail directory contains only the JRE runtime, application JAR, and an empty /tmp. The process runs under a dedicated UID (65534) with no supplementary groups. The container's network namespace has iptables OUTPUT chain rules restricting TCP connections to only 10.0.2.15:25 (internal Postfix MTA). The Postfix instance at 10.0.2.15 is configured with header_checks = pcre:/etc/postfix/header_checks.pcre containing '/^Subject:.*[\r\n]/ REJECT malformed_header' and smtpd_data_restrictions = reject_multi_recipient_bounce. Additionally, the Postfix milter chain includes opendkim-milter which rejects any message where the envelope-from domain does not match a DKIM-signed domain in the allow list. The combination of chroot confinement (no /etc/passwd, no /proc, no sensitive files to exfiltrate), network restriction to a single hardened MTA, and the MTA's own header injection detection via pcre header_checks means the CRLF injection in the subject field is neutralized at the SMTP layer before delivery.

config.runtime: JVM 17 in OCI container with pivot_root to /srv/jail
config.network_rules: iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 10.0.2.15 --dport 25 -j ACCEPT; iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -j DROP
config.postfix_milter: opendkim with strict envelope-from domain validation
config.filesystem: read-only rootfs, no /proc, no /etc/passwd, no sensitive data
